frequency_question: How often do US real GDP advance estimates print below 1.0% annualized when preceding quarters show similar leading indicator signals?
membership_rule: Members are BEA advance GDP release quarters for the United States from 1970 to present where annualized real GDP growth was below 1.0%. Excluded are revised estimates beyond the advance release.
provenance_note: claims 50 cases from only 7 named (7.1x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 7 explicitly named major sub-1.0% prints out of approximately 50 comparable soft indicator quarters since 1970.
known_gaps: Excludes minor revisions and focuses solely on the advance estimate print matching the target resolution criteria.
skeleton: Total quarters sampled since 1970 (~224 quarters total) divided by historical frequency of sub-1.0% advance prints.
multiplier: 7 sub-1.0% advance prints out of roughly 50 quarters exhibiting similar soft leading indicator configurations over 224 total quarters.
validity_reason: Macroeconomic data structures and BEA estimation methodologies remain stable across multi-year horizons.
